note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1936. Nominations closed on 5 May 1936. The Irish News of 6 May 1936, p. 7 prints the nominations for all nineteen divisions: eighteen single nominations, returned unopposed, and Granville, where the Unionist, Mr. Wm. Hall, was opposed by Mr. Robert Newton, D.L., chairman of the Dungannon Ratepayers' Association (also Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15). The Nationalists did not nominate for Clonavaddy and Coalisland. The Granville result has not been found, so Granville is not recorded. Bernagh is held: the Mid-Ulster Mail (9 May 1936, p. 9) reports a possible contest there, which the Irish News list does not show. Labels are as printed. Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Crossdernott' to Crossdernot (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the 1948 order naming Dungannon Rural District's nineteen divisions (Ministry of Health and Local Government, 26 August 1948; Belfast Gazette, 1 April 1949), the 1911 and 1930 DED maps (CROSSDERNOT) and the OSNI townland spell it Crossdernot. This round was filed under the spelling 'Crossdernott', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (crossdernott) answers with a redirect to this one.
